# Pelvic Floor Therapy

### Women's and Men's Health Specialists

Pelvic floor dysfunction comprises a range of issues for both women and men, often manifesting as urinary incontinence, pelvic pain, or sexual dysfunction. In women, it frequently stems from childbirth, menopause, or gynecological issues, while in men, it can result from prostate problems or surgery. Our team can compassionately address these sensitive conditions to reduce pain, restore function and improve your quality of life.

### Prenatal and Postpartum Care

Our physical therapists understand the unique changes that happen to the body during pregnancy, labor, and delivery. We also understand the challenges new mothers face as they nurture and care for their baby. We provide an individualized physical therapy experience through compassionate, one-on-one care combining manual techniques and exercise. Not only do we treat your symptoms, we also work with you to regain optimal health and strength after childbirth.

## Common prenatal and postpartum DIAGNOSES:

- Low back pain / SI pain
- Sacrotuberous ligament pain
- High or low pelvic floor tone
- Diastasis Recti
- Pelvic organ prolapse
- Postural dysfunction
- Gait dysfunction

![](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

### What to Expect During Pelvic Floor Physical Therapy

At DPT, our team ensures your safety and comfort at all times. We will do a thorough assessment to make sure we are doing our absolute best to help you get better, faster.

## SOME Treatment interventions may INCLUDE:

- Internal vaginal or rectal examination and treatment of the pelvic floor muscles
- Strengthening and re-training of weak muscles
- Relaxation of hyperactive or muscles in spasm
- Soft tissue mobilization to relieve tightness

## SOME CONDITIONS WE TREAT IN WOMEN AND MEN INCLUDE:

- Chronic Pelvic Pain
- Incontinence (Stress, Fecal, Urinary)
- Diastasis Recti
- Issues after Prostactectomy
- Sexual Dysfunction
- Coccygodynia
- Dyspareunia
- Low Back Pain
- Pain During and After Pregnancy
- Painful Bladder Syndrome (Interstitial Cystitis)
- Pelvic Organ Prolapse
- Urinary Urgency
- Pudendal Nerve Entrapment
- Vaginismus
- Vulvar Pain

## Ready To Start Feeling Better? Schedule Your Appointment Now!

No need to wait any longer to start feeling better! Get signed up now for an appointment now to get back to the life you love!

[Schedule Now](https://members.drsofpt.com/dpt/welcome)
